## Mean and SD

Can we check central limit theorem using simulations
```{r}
sim_mean_sd(n_obs = 30)
```

Let's do this but keep track of results
```{r}
output = vector("list", length = 1000)

for (i in 1:1000) {
  
  output[[i]] = sim_mean_sd(n_obs = 30)
}

# do the sim_mean_sd function 1000 times
```

Inspect results
```{r}
output |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
  summarize(
    emp_m = mean(mean),
    emp_se = sd(mean)
  )

# now have 1000 rows and 2 columns 

# empirical mean is the average of the 1000 means

# empirical sd is the sd of the 1000 means
```

```{r}
output |> 
  bind_rows() |> 
 ggplot(aes(x = mean))+
  geom_density()

# underlying data generating mechanism was a normal distribution, so plot looks normally distributed
```

Let's do this using tibbles and map instead!
```{r}
sim_results_df = 
  tibble(
    samp_size = rep(30, 1000)
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    est_df = map(samp_size, sim_mean_sd)
  ) |> 
  unnest(est_df)
```

Look at results
```{r}
sim_results_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = mean))+
  geom_density()
```

## Change 'n'
```{r}
sim_results_df = 
  expand_grid(
    samp_size = c(30, 60, 120, 240),
    iter = 1:1000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    est_df = map(samp_size, sim_mean_sd)
  ) |> 
  unnest(est_df)

# expand_grid creates a data frame that has all possible combinations of the inputs (here it is samp_size and iter) (so sample size 30 1000 times, sample size 60 1000 times, etc)
```

```{r}
sim_results_df |> 
  mutate(
    samp_size = str_c("n =", samp_size),
    # converts to character and for every row, it takes the text "n =" and combines it with whatever value is currently stored in samp_size
    samp_size = fct_inorder(samp_size)
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = samp_size, y = mean))+
  geom_violin()
```

Look at the numbers
```{r}
sim_results_df |> 
  mutate(
    samp_size = str_c("n =", samp_size),
    samp_size = fct_inorder(samp_size)
  ) |> 
  group_by(samp_size) |> 
    summarize(
    emp_m = mean(mean),
    emp_se = sd(mean)
  )
  
```

## Simple linear regression!!

generate once
```{r}
sim_data = tibble(
  x = rnorm(30, mean = 1, sd = 1),
  y = 2 + 3 * x + rnorm(30, mean = 0, sd = 1)
)

# sim_data |> 
#  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y))+
# geom_point() +
#  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE)


  fit = lm(y~x, data = sim_data)
  fit
```
Turn this into a function
(i did that, it is in `source/sim_slr.R`)

This works once:
```{r}
sim_slr(30)
```

Do this a lot!!
```{r}
slr_results_df =
  tibble(
    samp_size = rep(30, 1000)
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    est_df = map(samp_size, sim_slr)
  ) |> 
  unnest(est_df)
```


Look at the results
```{r}
slr_results_df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = beta0_hat, y = beta1_hat))+
  geom_point()

#estimated intercept and estimated slope are negatively correlated with each other
```

## birthday problem

```{r}
birthdays = sample(1:365, size = 5, replace = TRUE)
# a draw of 5 birthdays
# replace = TRUE makes it so that you can draw the same numbers multiple times

repeated_birthdays = length(unique(birthdays)) < 5

repeated_birthdays
```
Turn this into a function

run it a bunch
```{r}
birthday_repeated(147)
```

run it a bunch but good
```{r}
birthday_results_df =
  expand_grid(
    number_of_people = 5:50,
    iter = 1:1000
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    repeated = map_lgl(number_of_people, birthday_repeated)
  )

# map_lgl unnests the logical variable
```

look at these results
```{r}
birthday_results_df |> 
  group_by(number_of_people) |> 
  summarize(prob_of_repeat = mean(repeated)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = number_of_people, y = prob_of_repeat)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line()
```
